title: Controlled Engram portability study
question: Can the exact same frozen Engram artifact transfer useful information to independently configured DenseLM recipient backbones, including different hidden widths, using only a small recipient-local alignment adapter?
mechanisms: token, raw-byte, and structured semantic addressing
hypothesis: Under matched recipient preparation and controls, a real frozen artifact may improve declared recipient behavior over no-memory, random-memory, and row-corruption controls; it may also fail to do so.
failure_interpretation: A null or adverse controlled contrast means this bounded protocol did not demonstrate useful recipient-local adaptation for that representation, recipient, task family, or endpoint; it does not establish that retrieval was unavailable or that a different architecture would behave identically.
controls: Use the same independently prepared recipient backbone and recipient-local adapter initialization within each matched recipient/condition group.
Keep the frozen real artifact byte-identical across recipient widths for each declared source/representation group; retain its digest and pack identity.

Compare no-memory, random frozen memory, real frozen memory at step zero, adapter-only real memory, joint recipient training, native recipient memory, and row-association corruption as separately named conditions.
Keep source facts, recipient preparation facts, adapter eligibility, development observations, and final replacement worlds separated and auditable.
Report retrieval-only oracle diagnostics separately from unrestricted recipient answer behavior.
independent_variables: memory condition and recipient-local trainable set
confounders: Token-address compatibility is an address invariant, not hidden-coordinate compatibility.
Raw-byte endpoint agreement does not establish behavioral equivalence across tokenizers.
Structured semantic queries are pre-encoded caller-supplied vectors in this protocol, not a supported natural-language query production path.
Exact key/value encoder identities, dimensions, normalization, and representation-space identity are required semantic interface invariants; a shared tokenizer is insufficient.
Different width/depth recipients are dense-attention DenseLM variants, not a cross-architecture experiment.
Recipient behavior can differ from exact retrieval; scorer traversal must not repair a wrong neural intermediate prediction.
Native-memory arms have different fact exposure and optimization budgets and are not matched adapter-only causal contrasts.
hardware_notes: The declared portability campaign requires explicit generated worlds, source artifacts, recipient preparation checkpoints, and verified protocol assets. Measure setup, compilation, observation, checkpoint, and update costs on the selected backend; this packaged entry contains no timing or behavioral measurements.
runtime_class: A bounded multi-seed PyTorch research protocol with immutable artifacts and typed observations; no portability result has been measured by this catalog entry.

applicability.offline: diagnostic only; not a portability outcome
diagnostic only; not a replacement-world score
diagnostic only; not a structured conflict trace

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.claim_boundary: Background on retrieval-augmented systems only; it is not evidence that this protocol transfers an Engram or that its recipient behavior succeeds.

can_establish: Observed controlled recipient behavior for the executed artifacts, tasks, seeds, DenseLM widths, and endpoints.
Whether exact artifact bytes and structured pack identities remained unchanged across recipient configurations.
Recipient answer/path accuracy at immutable checkpoints, structured retrieval traces, and bounded A/B/A attachment responses.
cannot_establish: Any portability success claim beyond the specific executed observations.
Natural-language semantic query production, because structured queries are supplied by the generator.
That direct retrieval is recipient behavioral success, or that a correct retrieval trace repairs a recipient prediction.
Cross-architecture portability, broad knowledge transfer, cross-tokenizer behavioral equivalence, or zero-shot language competence.
prerequisites: Build an explicit versioned campaign before training; the portability CLI binds generated worlds, verified assets, recipient preparation checkpoints, and typed observations.
The packaged default recipe remains an inert generic configuration sketch; it does not substitute for the portability campaign or its supplied structured queries, replacements, and evaluator.
